litigation.note: The Company's land at Thergaon, Pune is, in the Government's contention, still subject to the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, which is contrary to the legal opinion received by the Company. The matter is pending with the Government authorities after an order of the Bombay High Court that directed disposal in a time-bound manner; given the long delay at the Government level the Company may have to again approach the Hon'ble High Court. The consequence is that the 'GREEN VILLE' project continues to be on hold. Separately, the Directors' Report states there is no adverse remark or qualification in the Statutory Auditor's Report or the Secretarial Audit Report, and the Auditors reported no fraud on or by the Company during the year. risks.note: The Government contends the Company's land continues to be subject to the repealed Urban Land Ceiling Act, contrary to the legal opinion received by the Company. The matter is pending with Government authorities after the Bombay High Court ordered time-bound disposal, and the Company may have to again approach the High Court. This land underpins both the leased Thergaon property and (per sibling bundles) the stalled 'GREEN VILLE' project, so an adverse outcome would impair a core asset.
risks.risk: Land-title / Urban Land Ceiling Act dispute over the Thergaon, Pune land

risks.note: 'The sector faces competition particularly from the areas nearby the Company's project' - competing supply is located adjacent to the Company's own development, so it bears on pricing and absorption of the GREENS towers directly.
risks.risk: Competition in the Pune residential market

risks.note: 'Although the demand by and large remains fairly stable, the larger supply and inflation does put pressures at times on demand' - management explicitly flags episodic demand pressure despite broadly stable underlying demand.

The redevelopment segment, which management positions as the future growth pipeline, 'faces stiff competition from developers offering increasingly higher free area and compensation' - i.e. winning mandates requires giving away more area/compensation, compressing developer economics.
risks.risk: Stiff competition for society redevelopment mandates

risks.note: 'The Company's business comprises of real estate development for housing project in and around Pune' with the wind mills in Maharashtra and the leased property at Thergaon, Pune - a structural geographic concentration, disclosed as fact rather than labelled as a risk.
risks.risk: Single-geography concentration - the entire housing business is in and around Pune

risks.note: 'The real estate development is carried out through its subsidiaries, namely; AMJ Land Developers, a firm in which the Company holds 95% stake and wholly owned subsidiary Company, AMJ Realty Ltd.' - the listed company's real-estate earnings depend on entities it does not wholly own in one case (95% firm).
risks.risk: Execution concentrated in subsidiary/partnership vehicles rather than the listed entity

risks.note: 'Two of these wind mills are situated on the forest land leased out to the Company' - two of the three wind mills (of the aggregate 4.6 MW) sit on leased forest land rather than owned land, creating tenure/renewal dependence.
risks.risk: Wind assets partly dependent on leased forest land
